cs.AI / 1 / 2611.33394
Confidence scores for gated automation of large language models
用于大型语言模型门控自动化的置信度分数
Luiz G. A. Alves, Aaron Vermeersch
cs.AI · cs.CL · cs.LG
large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
AI agents built on large language models (LLMs) demonstrate strong capabilities in automated decision-making. However, LLMs may produce incorrect answers with high confidence, limiting their applicability in decisions that affect individuals and organizations. Reliable confidence scores are necessary to gate such decisions, and existing estimates are frequently unavailable or too coarse to support effective gating. This work uses supervised learning to train models to predict the correctness of LLM-generated answers, enabling automated confident responses and routing uncertain ones for human review. A linear confidence score head is fitted to the final-layer hidden state of the frozen LLM backbone, and text-only metamodels are trained as an alternative for closed models. All results come from a single 2B-parameter backbone, on graded answers that are about 98% SQuAD and the remainder TruthfulQA. Against multiple baselines, the confidence score head outperforms all baselines and metamodels, automating the largest fraction of the workload at high accuracy targets. Prompted confidence scores can appear well calibrated yet lack the resolution needed for thresholding. Although transferability to unseen datasets is modest, the confidence score head remains the most robust approach. The proposed confidence scoring framework enhances the safety of automating LLM-based agents and can be adapted to gate other properties, including safety or compliance.
Chinese Translation
基于大型语言模型（LLM）构建的 AI 智能体在自动化决策中展现出强大的能力。然而，LLM 可能以高置信度产生错误答案，这限制了它们在影响个人和组织的决策中的适用性。可靠的置信度分数对于对此类决策进行门控是必要的，而现有估计往往不可用或过于粗糙，无法支持有效的门控。本工作使用监督学习训练模型来预测 LLM 生成答案的正确性，从而实现有信心的自动响应，并将不确定的响应转交人工审查。一个线性置信度分数头被拟合到冻结的 LLM 骨干的最后一层隐藏状态上，并且训练纯文本元模型作为封闭模型的替代方案。所有结果均来自一个单一的 20 亿参数骨干，基于分级答案，其中约 98% 为 SQuAD，其余为 TruthfulQA。在多个基线对比下，置信度分数头优于所有基线和元模型，在高准确率目标下自动化了最大比例的工作负载。提示得到的置信度分数可能看起来校准良好，却缺乏阈值化所需的分辨率。尽管对未见数据集的迁移性有限，置信度分数头仍然是最稳健的方法。所提出的置信度评分框架增强了自动化基于 LLM 的智能体的安全性，并且可以调整用于门控其他属性，包括安全性或合规性。

cs.AI / 2 / 2611.33470
Dynamic Reasoning in Next-Gen Detection and Response: An Empirical Study of LLM Triage, Reinforcement Tuning, and Adversarial Evasion
下一代检测与响应中的动态推理：关于 LLM 分诊、强化微调与对抗规避的实证研究
Jeremy Canale
cs.AI · cs.CR
large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
We present an end-to-end empirical study of dynamic reasoning in next-generation detection and response pipelines, evaluating how static classifiers, graph-based signal fusion, and large language model (LLM) triage agents perform under strict human-analyst attention budgets (Recall at B alerts/day). Across 56 reproducible experiments spanning a multi-layer enterprise-and-cloud simulator and four public datasets (SOREL-20M, BODMAS, LANL, and DARPA Transparent Computing), we test twelve architectural claims governing modern fleet-scale defense. First, we show that fleet growth halves recall at a fixed analyst budget even at negligible compute cost (<$0.0003 per million events), and that rarity-weighted graph risk propagation outperforms GraphSAGE without neural training. Second, evaluating frontier reasoning models (Gemini) and fine-tuned open-weight models (Qwen3-4B) for alert triage reveals that unconstrained LLM auto-closure eliminates 90% of false positives while silently discarding 31-44% of true attack cases. Third, post-training with Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) causes severe reward hacking on unseen attack classes, suppressing up to 86% of novel attacks compared to two-epoch supervised fine-tuning. Finally, against an adaptive adversary generating plausible cover stories in benign telemetry fields, LLM triage evasion rises sharply unless gated by a deterministic policy harness prior to model invocation.

我们呈现了一项关于下一代检测与响应流水线中动态推理的端到端实证研究，评估静态分类器、基于图的信号融合以及大语言模型（LLM）分诊代理在严格的人类分析师注意力预算（每日 B 条告警下的召回率）下表现如何。跨越多层企业—云模拟器和四个公开数据集（SOREL-20M、BODMAS、LANL 和 DARPA Transparent Computing）的 56 个可复现实验，我们检验了支配现代机群规模防御的十二项架构性主张。首先，我们表明即使在计算成本可忽略不计（每百万事件 <$0.0003）的情况下，机群增长也会使固定分析师预算下的召回率减半，并且稀有性加权的图风险传播在无需神经训练的情况下优于 GraphSAGE。其次，针对告警分诊评估前沿推理模型（Gemini）和微调后的开放权重模型（Qwen3-4B）后发现，无约束的 LLM 自动关闭可消除 90% 的误报，但同时静默丢弃 31-44% 的真实攻击案例。第三，使用组相对策略优化（GRPO）进行后训练会在未见攻击类别上导致严重的奖励黑客行为，与两轮监督微调相比，最多可抑制 86% 的新型攻击。最后，面对在良性遥测字段中生成看似可信的掩护故事的 adaptive 对手时，除非在调用模型之前由确定性策略约束框架进行门控，否则 LLM 分诊规避率会急剧上升。

cs.AI / 3 / 2611.33563
FIG-MAC: A Fine-grained Inspiration Graph Empowered Multi-Agent Collaboration for Automated Scientific Hypothesis Generation
FIG-MAC：一种面向自动化科学假设生成的细粒度灵感图赋能的多智能体协作方法
Siyuan Chen, Yuping Gao, Tai Huang, Yuling Zhou, Dongyu Su, Tongguan Wang
cs.AI
large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
Automated Scientific Hypothesis Generation (ASHG) leveraging large language models (LLMs) aims to harness their strengths in knowledge integration, logical reasoning, and text generation for efficiently producing innovative, verifiable scientific hypotheses. However, existing approaches face three critical limitations: (i) insufficient fine-grained knowledge representation, as unstructured context impairs LLM comprehension and reasoning; (ii) lack of knowledge evolution traceability, constraining the generation of innovative cross-domain conjectures; (iii) absence of human-inspired and role-specialized multi-agent collaboration, failing to leverage the efficient innovation mechanisms arising from cognitive diversity and division of labor among expert roles to complete the full ASHG-evaluation loop. To address these limitations, we propose the Fine-grained Inspiration Graph-empowered Multi-Agent Collaboration framework (FIG-MAC) including: (i) Fine-grained Inspiration Graph module (FIG), to obtain fine-grained structured knowledge representations, where nodes represent academic semantic units and edges encode heuristic relationships among them; (ii) ontology-guided hybrid reasoning module, which follows the FIG ontology to construct structured reasoning paths and uses vector search to enrich them with semantic evidence, to obtain the traceable scientific conjecture paths; (iii) role-specialized Multi-Agent framework, inspired by real scientific teamwork, enabling a closed-loop process of scientific conjecture generation, screening, and validation. Experimental results demonstrate that FIG-MAC significantly outperforms state-of-the-art methods on source diversity, provenance-adjusted novelty, and raw novelty.
Chinese Translation
利用大语言模型（LLMs）的自动化科学假设生成（ASHG）旨在发挥其在知识整合、逻辑推理和文本生成方面的优势，以高效地产出创新且可验证的科学假设。然而，现有方法面临三个关键局限：（i）细粒度知识表示不足，因为非结构化上下文会损害LLM的理解和推理能力；（ii）缺乏知识演化可追溯性，制约了创新性跨域猜想的生成；（iii）缺乏受人类启发且角色专业化的多智能体协作，未能利用专家角色之间认知多样性和分工所产生的高效创新机制来完成完整的ASHG—评估闭环。为解决这些局限，我们提出细粒度灵感图赋能的多智能体协作框架（FIG-MAC），包括：（i）细粒度灵感图模块（FIG），用于获得细粒度的结构化知识表示，其中节点表示学术语义单元，边编码它们之间的启发式关系；（ii）本体引导的混合推理模块，该模块遵循FIG本体构建结构化推理路径，并使用向量搜索以语义证据丰富这些路径，从而获得可追溯的科学猜想路径；（iii）角色专业化的多智能体框架，受真实科学团队合作启发，实现科学猜想生成、筛选和验证的闭环过程。实验结果表明，FIG-MAC在来源多样性、来源调整新颖性和原始新颖性方面显著优于最先进的方法。

cs.AI / 4 / 2611.33679
Faster and Better Query (FBQ): Learning Future-Position Probes from the First Generated Token
更快更好的查询（FBQ）：从第一个生成 token 学习未来位置探针
Jiankun Zou, Daixing Chen, Tongtong Yuan
cs.AI
large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
When a large language model (LLM) evicts prompt keys and values at the end of prefill, it must decide what to keep before it sees the queries from subsequent decoding steps. Generating a draft continuation can approximate those queries at the cost of extra autoregressive steps. Can we use the embedding of the first output token, already available from the final prefill logits, to construct low-cost pseudo queries that approximate future decoding queries? We start with FTQ-8, which places eight copies of the first token ID at consecutive future positions and reads their attention to the prompt in one causal forward pass. Each copy sees a different prefix, but a generic opening such as the offers a poor literal guess for seven successive tokens. Faster and Better Query (FBQ) preserves the first embedding and learns an additive offset at each of the seven remaining positions. We train these offsets to predict the average prompt attention of a full-cache continuation. On LongBench, FBQ performs comparably to eight-step Lookahead Q-Cache at the same cache budget, using a single forward pass to compute all probe queries.
Chinese Translation
当大型语言模型（LLM）在预填充结束时驱逐提示键和值时，它必须在看到后续解码步骤的查询之前决定保留什么。生成一个草稿续写可以以额外的自回归步骤为代价来近似这些查询。我们能否利用第一个输出 token 的嵌入——它已经可以从最终的预填充 logits 中获得——来构造低成本的伪查询，以近似未来的解码查询？我们从 FTQ-8 开始，它将第一个 token ID 的八个副本放置在连续的未来位置上，并在一次因果前向传播中读取它们对提示的注意力。每个副本看到不同的前缀，但像 the 这样的通用开头对于七个连续 token 来说只能提供很差的字面猜测。更快更好的查询（FBQ）保留第一个嵌入，并在其余七个位置中的每一个位置学习一个加性偏移。我们训练这些偏移，以预测全缓存续写的平均提示注意力。在 LongBench 上，FBQ 在相同缓存预算下与八步 Lookahead Q-Cache 表现相当，并使用单次前向传播计算所有探针查询。

cs.AI / 5 / 2611.33706
EVA: Evidence-seeking Visual Agent for Hallucination-Resistant Multimodal Reasoning
EVA：用于抗幻觉多模态推理的证据寻求视觉智能体
Ting Lei, Yu Chen, Yang Liu
cs.AI
large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
Hallucinations in multimodal large language models (MLLMs) often arise from visual assumptions that go unchecked. Self-reflection, multi-agent debate, and counterfactual verification can reinforce erroneous conclusions when they rely on the same unverified visual assumptions. External visual tools can provide verifiable evidence, but models may select the wrong tools, supply incorrect parameters, or ignore or contradict the evidence they obtain. In this work, we propose EVA, an Evidence-seeking Visual Agent that reframes multimodal reasoning as an explicit process of evidence acquisition and verification. At the core of EVA is a unified evidence-grounded execution pipeline designed to address the above challenges through two tightly coupled mechanisms. First, we introduce Iterative Tool Replanning, which dynamically refines tool selection and parameters based on intermediate observations, improving the reliability of tool usage. Second, we develop Evidence Consistency Verification, an answer validation mechanism that improves alignment between the final prediction and the collected evidence, mitigating evidence--reasoning inconsistencies. In addition, to balance robustness and efficiency, EVA incorporates Selective Evidence Routing, an adaptive fast--slow reasoning strategy that determines when external evidence is necessary. Visually straightforward queries are handled via direct reasoning, while complex or high-risk cases trigger tool-based evidence acquisition. By jointly addressing how to reliably acquire evidence and how to use it consistently, EVA transforms multimodal reasoning from passive answer validation into explicit evidence-backed decision making. Experimental results demonstrate that EVA achieves significantly improved reasoning reliability over direct VLM inference and multi-agent methods, while maintaining efficiency through selective tool invocation.
Chinese Translation
多模态大语言模型（MLLMs）中的幻觉常常源于未经检验的视觉假设。当自我反思、多智能体辩论和反事实验证依赖于相同的未经核实的视觉假设时，它们可能会强化错误结论。外部视觉工具可以提供可验证的证据，但模型可能会选择错误的工具、提供不正确的参数，或者忽略或抵触其获得的证据。在本工作中，我们提出 EVA，一种证据寻求视觉智能体，它将多模态推理重构为一个显式的证据获取与验证过程。EVA 的核心是一个统一的、基于证据的执行流水线，旨在通过两个紧密耦合的机制应对上述挑战。首先，我们引入迭代工具重规划（Iterative Tool Replanning），它基于中间观察动态细化工具选择和参数，提高工具使用的可靠性。其次，我们开发证据一致性验证（Evidence Consistency Verification），这是一种答案验证机制，可改善最终预测与所收集证据之间的一致性，缓解证据--推理不一致。此外，为了平衡鲁棒性与效率，EVA 引入选择性证据路由（Selective Evidence Routing），这是一种自适应快--慢推理策略，用于确定何时需要外部证据。视觉上直截了当的查询通过直接推理处理，而复杂或高风险案例则触发基于工具的证据获取。通过共同解决如何可靠地获取证据以及如何一致地使用证据，EVA 将多模态推理从被动的答案验证转变为显式的、有证据支持的决策。实验结果表明，EVA 相较直接 VLM 推理和多智能体方法显著提高了推理可靠性，同时通过选择性工具调用保持效率。

cs.AI / 6 / 2611.33712
PowerFix: Physics-Guided Iterative Repair for LLM-Assisted Power Converter Design
PowerFix：面向LLM辅助功率变换器设计的物理引导迭代修复
Can Wang, Shi Qiu, Fanfan Lin
cs.AI
large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
Large language model (LLM) agents are increasingly being explored for automated engineering design. However, repairing power-converter designs that fail engineering validation remains challenging: the system must identify physical causes, locate responsible design variables, and resolve violations without compromising other constraints. We introduce PowerFix, a physics-guided iterative repair framework that converts validation failures into structured diagnoses and executable patches while preserving topology and design requirements. PowerDiagGraph links failed checks to possible physical causes and constrains repair routes. An LLM prioritizes these routes, while a deterministic compiler translates selected repairs into authorized field-level edits. Candidates are validated on isolated design copies and committed only after all required engineering checks pass; failed validation can guide replanning. On our constructed 96-task flyback repair benchmark, comprising injected single faults, coupled faults, and held-out natural failures from our design generator, PowerFix achieves 78.7% verified repair success rate (VRSR), compared with 30.1% for the strongest of three LLM baselines. Three additional replanning rounds increase VRSR to 88.4%. These offline results provide pilot-stage evidence within a simulation-based design workflow, with hardware prototype validation and transfer to a second converter topology as the next steps toward deployment.
Chinese Translation
大型语言模型（LLM）智能体正日益被探索用于自动化工程设计。然而，修复未通过工程验证的功率变换器设计仍然具有挑战性：系统必须识别物理原因、定位导致问题的设计变量，并在不损害其他约束的情况下解决违规。我们提出PowerFix，一个物理引导的迭代修复框架，它将验证失败转化为结构化诊断和可执行补丁，同时保持拓扑和设计要求。PowerDiagGraph将失败的检查与可能的物理原因关联起来，并约束修复路径。LLM对这些路径进行优先级排序，而确定性编译器将选定的修复转换为授权的字段级编辑。候选方案在隔离的设计副本上进行验证，并且仅在所有必需的工程检查通过后才提交；验证失败可以指导重新规划。在我们构建的96任务反激式修复基准上（该基准包含注入的单故障、耦合故障以及来自我们设计生成器的留出自然故障），PowerFix达到78.7%的验证修复成功率（VRSR），而三个LLM基线中最强者的成功率为30.1%。额外的三轮重新规划将VRSR提高到88.4%。这些离线结果为基于仿真的设计工作流程提供了试点阶段证据，而硬件原型验证以及迁移到第二种变换器拓扑是迈向部署的下一步。

cs.AI / 7 / 2611.33735
JOVE ICE: Intent Guided Cloud Edge Device Collaboration for AI Glasses
JOVE ICE：面向 AI 眼镜的意图引导云边端协同
Yuyang Jin, Bingfeng Pi, Jiamei Sun, Wei Jin, Dongyang Wang, Yunpeng Li, Yan Bai, Lei Zuo
cs.AI
large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
Recent advances in large language models (LLMs) and LLM based agents have expanded the capabilities of AI glasses, enabling egocentric visual question answering, memory retrieval, and proactive assistance. These applications involve diverse inputs, including speech, images, and video, and range from simple device control to complex visual reasoning, posing challenges for efficient computation and communication. While video centric capabilities have received considerable attention, simple text based and device executable tasks remain underexplored despite their prevalence in daily interactions. Efficiently supporting diverse workloads within a unified assistant remains an open challenge. We propose JOVE ICE, an intent guided cloud, edge, and device collaborative framework that routes requests among AI glasses, a paired smartphone, and cloud servers according to user intent. JOVE ICE integrates hierarchical intent classification with dynamic subagent orchestration to select efficient execution paths and flexibly incorporate new applications through specialized subagents. Analysis of real world AI glasses requests reveals that simple device control tasks account for over 30% of interactions, which JOVE ICE handles directly on device to avoid unnecessary cloud computation and costs. Evaluations on three public benchmarks demonstrate that JOVE ICE reduces time to first token by approximately 13% and token usage by over 11% compared with conventional device and cloud architectures, while maintaining task quality. These results demonstrate the potential of intent guided collaboration to improve the efficiency and scalability of AI glasses.
Chinese Translation
大语言模型（LLM）及基于 LLM 的智能体的最新进展扩展了 AI 眼镜的能力，使其能够实现第一人称视觉问答、记忆检索和主动辅助。这些应用涉及包括语音、图像和视频在内的多种输入，并且从简单的设备控制到复杂的视觉推理不等，对高效计算与通信提出了挑战。尽管以视频为中心的能力已受到相当多的关注，但简单的基于文本的任务和可由设备执行的任务尽管在日常交互中十分普遍，却仍未得到充分探索。在统一的助手内高效支持多样化工作负载仍是一个开放挑战。我们提出 JOVE ICE，一个意图引导的云、边、端协同框架，它根据用户意图在 AI 眼镜、配对智能手机和云服务器之间路由请求。JOVE ICE 将分层意图分类与动态子智能体编排相结合，以选择高效的执行路径，并通过专用子智能体灵活集成新应用。对真实世界 AI 眼镜请求的分析表明，简单的设备控制任务占交互的 30% 以上，JOVE ICE 直接在设备上处理这些任务，以避免不必要的云端计算和成本。在三个公开基准上的评估表明，与传统设备和云架构相比，JOVE ICE 将首 token 时间缩短约 13%，将 token 使用量降低 11% 以上，同时保持任务质量。这些结果证明了意图引导协作在提升 AI 眼镜效率与可扩展性方面的潜力。

cs.AI / 8 / 2611.33748
REFORGE: LLM-Assisted RTL Bug Repair with Structured Context and Verification Feedback
REFORGE：利用结构化上下文与验证反馈的 LLM 辅助 RTL 缺陷修复
Tanvir Hossain, Sudipta Paria, Aidan Gleason Myers, Swarup Bhunia, Tamzidul Hoque
cs.AI · cs.SE
large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
Large language models (LLMs) can write and repair RTL, but successful compilation or testbench execution does not establish defect removal, behavioral preservation, security, or implementation feasibility. Existing LLM-based RTL repair methods often report a single repair rate without retaining separate evidence for these properties, limiting reproducible comparison and integration into hardware design flows. We present REFORGE, which, to our knowledge, is the first LLM-assisted RTL repair framework that maintains and accumulates structured repair evidence across iterations, allowing it to generate fixes that satisfy multiple objectives simultaneously, including functionality, behavioral equivalence, security, and cost efficiency. REFORGE profiles buggy RTL, identifies structural and security-relevant features, localizes failing behavior, and uses verification-guided diagnosis to generate complete RTL repair variants. Each variant undergoes syntax checking, simulation, formal analysis, off-trigger preservation, security re-scan, and synthesis-based power, performance, and area analysis. We implement REFORGE as a backend-independent repair-and-verification flow and evaluate it in 288 runs across three LLM backends and three benchmark suites. On CirFix, the proposed context and diagnosis increase runs delivering a checked repair from 32/63 to 51/63, while every configuration repairs the Hack@DAC OpenTitan defect. Evidence records also show that a testbench-only criterion reports 3.9 times more repairs than the full set of applicable checks, security-clean outputs may lack functional verification, and different RTL repairs can implement equivalent hardware. These results show that LLM-generated RTL repairs require explicit multi-stage verification evidence rather than a single pass/fail outcome.

大型语言模型（LLM）能够编写和修复 RTL，但成功编译或 testbench 执行并不能证明缺陷已被移除、行为得到保持、安全性或实现可行性。现有的基于 LLM 的 RTL 修复方法通常只报告单一的修复率，而不保留针对这些属性的独立证据，从而限制了可复现的比较以及集成到硬件设计流程中。我们提出 REFORGE；据我们所知，它是首个在迭代过程中维护并累积结构化修复证据的 LLM 辅助 RTL 修复框架，使其能够生成同时满足多个目标的修复，包括功能、行为等价性、安全性和成本效率。REFORGE 对有缺陷的 RTL 进行剖析，识别结构与安全相关特征，定位失效行为，并使用验证引导的诊断来生成完整的 RTL 修复变体。每个变体都要经历语法检查、仿真、形式分析、非触发保持、安全性重新扫描，以及基于综合的功耗、性能和面积分析。我们将 REFORGE 实现为一种与后端无关的修复与验证流程，并在三个 LLM 后端和三个基准套件上的 288 次运行中对其进行评估。在 CirFix 上，所提出的上下文与诊断将产出经检查修复的运行数从 32/63 提高到 51/63，而每种配置都修复了 Hack@DAC OpenTitan 缺陷。证据记录还表明，仅基于 testbench 的判据报告的修复数比全套适用检查多 3.9 倍，安全性无问题的输出可能缺乏功能验证，并且不同的 RTL 修复可以实现等价的硬件。这些结果表明，LLM 生成的 RTL 修复需要明确的多阶段验证证据，而不是单一的通过/失败结果。

Abstract
Objective: To develop and validate InterGenEHR$^+$, an interactive framework for natural language-conditioned generation of synthetic tabular electronic health records (EHRs) and longitudinal trajectories for scenario-based evaluation of machine learning models. Methods: An optional large language model (LLM) parser converts clinical requests into structured constraints. Conditional variational autoencoders and diffusion models generate single-time-point records, while diffusion models generate longitudinal trajectories. We evaluate parsing, distributional fidelity, imputation, clinical-constraint adherence, mortality prediction, and clinical plausibility using a multi-institutional cohort of 874 patients receiving venovenous extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (VV-ECMO). Results: Gemma 3 4B with few-shot prompting achieves the highest parsing performance with a low spurious slot rate. IGE-TabDDPM and IGE-PMVAE perform well in single-time-point generation; IGE-CSDI, IGE-FGTI, and IGE-MTSCI lead on different longitudinal fidelity metrics. Across five random seeds and three classifiers, synthetic cohorts retain predictive utility for mortality prediction on real test data. Clinician ratings support trajectory plausibility and alignment with requested scenarios. Conclusion: InterGenEHR$^+$ supports clinician-specified generation of EHR trajectories with statistical fidelity and downstream predictive utility in the evaluated VV-ECMO cohort. Extension to other clinical settings requires further validation. Significance: The framework supports scenario-based evaluation of machine learning models in data-sparse critical care settings.

Can Its Own Misses Teach an MLLM to Find Small Brain Metastases?
它自身的漏检能否教会一个 MLLM 发现小的脑转移瘤？
Yixuan Duan, Kexin Geng, Hanwen Xu, Wei Qiu
cs.AI
large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) are becoming general readers of medical images, yet they remain weak at locating small abnormalities. Brain metastases expose this gap: at 384 px a 0.1 mL lesion covers less than a quarter of one visual token, and at one false positive per scan frontier MLLMs find fewer than 30% of lesions of 0.1-1 mL. Fine-tuning on one dataset helps but transfers poorly, and improving it further is slow trial and error steered by a single score. We introduce LANTERN (Lesion-finding AgeNt Through Error-driven Recursive learNing), a framework in which an MLLM improves recursively from its own misses. LANTERN recasts model development as an error-driven loop: a failure census attributes every missed lesion to one of four causes, an LLM mentor revises one of four levels (evidence acquisition, visual representation, learning policy, decision aggregation) per round, and a rule frozen before the first round decides what is kept, without test data and with every tool call audited. Over 15 unattended rounds, LANTERN raises a fine-tuned 4B MLLM from finding 75% to 94% of lesions at one false positive per scan on BraTS-MET, and 91% of those of 0.1-1 mL, compared with at most 51% and 29% for five frontier MLLMs read under the starting protocol; the gains hold on an external cohort (89%) and on unseen meningiomas (77%). These results show that an MLLM's own misses, attributed to their causes, can drive its reliable recursive self-improvement.

EATS: Scaling Tool-Use Experience for Medical Reasoning Agents
EATS：为医疗推理智能体扩展工具使用经验
Mingyuan Li, Tong Jia, Haoran Wang, Wenbo Qi, Ziyuan Yang, Bowen Ma, Jie Gui, Baosheng Yu
cs.AI
large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
Medical reasoning agents combine large language model (LLM) reasoning with clinical workflows and specialized neural tools. However, general-purpose LLMs receive limited training exposure to domain-specific medical tools, and the uncertainty and distributional shifts of neural tool outputs make selecting tools from simple descriptions significantly more challenging than in deterministic settings such as calculators or dictionary lookups. In this paper, we propose EATS, an experience-augmented tool selection strategy that leverages accumulated tool-use trajectories to improve tool selection in medical reasoning agents. EATS constructs a memory of past interactions, including queries, tool choices, arguments, and self-evaluated feedback, and retrieves relevant experiences to guide tool selection for new queries. As memory construction does not require ground-truth supervision, EATS scales naturally with test-time experience. We evaluate EATS on tool-augmented medical reasoning tasks, including closed-ended visual question answering and free-form report generation. Experiments on four public datasets, ChestAgentBench, CheXbench, MIMIC-CXR, and SLAKE-VQA, across three multimodal LLMs, Qwen3-VL 2B, Qwen3-VL 32B, and GPT-5.5, show consistent gains in tool selection behavior and downstream medical reasoning performance. Code is available at https://github.com/Limingyuan001/EATS.

PatternMiner: Automated Mathematical Discovery Through LLM-Guided Training and Interpretation of Small Models
PatternMiner：通过LLM引导的小模型训练与解释实现自动化数学发现
Michael Ruofan Zeng, Junaid Hasan, Xuanyu Yang, Emily Xia Meng, Henry Kvinge
cs.AI · math.CO
large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
There are several approaches to AI-driven mathematical discovery. One of these involves the use of large language models (LLMs) to resolve well-specified conjectures via text-based reasoning, while another uses narrow models and interpretability for more open-ended, human-in-the-loop exploration using object-based mathematical data. The latter is limited in its ability to move beyond simple empirical pattern detection while the former is not well-designed for direct, open-ended exploration of large mathematical datasets. In this paper we introduce PatternMiner, a system that combines these two paradigms. In PatternMiner, an LLM agent generates mathematical datasets based on an initial broad question, trains narrow machine learning models on them, uses interpretability techniques to extract patterns from these trained models, and uses these patterns to formulate conjectures. Once an initial conjecture has been formulated, PatternMiner instructs the agent to search for counterexamples using calls to mathematical software. If a set of counterexamples can be found, these are used as feedback for conjecture refinement or another round of training and interpretability. The conjecture progressively evolves through this iterative sequence with the agent allowed to try to prove it at any point. We describe the results of applying PatternMiner to five well-known positivity problems in algebraic combinatorics. PatternMiner proves several new theorems related to Schubert positivity and projection, a character-row evaluation formula, a restricted version of the Kazhdan--Lusztig combinatorial invariance conjecture, and Schur positivity for a family of immanant coefficients. We end by analyzing the most common routes to conjecture generation that are used by PatternMiner in our case studies as well as documenting the most common failure modes.

SOLO: Towards Sample-Faithful and Detectable LLM Watermarking under Repeated Sampling via Content-Anchored Single-Owner Contexts
SOLO：通过内容锚定的单一所有者上下文实现重复采样下样本保真且可检测的 LLM 水印
Zhongliang Guo, Yan Lin, Yifei Qian, Shuai Zhao, Luwei Xiao, Daizong Liu, Chun Pong Lau
cs.AI · cs.CL
large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
Providers watermark the outputs of large language models, while applications sample many responses per prompt for self-consistency, best-of-n selection, and uncertainty estimation. We show that deployed configurations of distortion-free watermarks, which deduplicate keyed contexts only within a response, couple the responses of a request: answer templates make all responses query the watermark with the same context before the answer, so collisions across responses, usually assumed rare, become the norm. Key pools reduce or avoid the coupling at the cost of multiple testing, and the exact remedy of a context history shared across the request leaves many positions unwatermarked. We propose SOLO, which keeps a request-scoped context history but anchors its keyed contexts on content selected by min-hash, so that siblings rarely compete for a context and random edits stay local. Its responses are jointly distributed as independent unwatermarked responses, each detectable with a single key. On five language models from three families and three benchmarks, SOLO preserves self-consistency and uncertainty estimation and, at a 1% false positive rate, detects more responses than four-token key pools on most tasks, also after randomly editing 10% of the tokens, and more than the context history on most clean tasks. Code is available at https://github.com/ZhongliangGuo/solo-watermark.

large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
AI systems increasingly help decide which drug targets enter costly clinical trials. We recast each target-disease hypothesis as a dated event, the pair's first clinical trial. This lets us test whether a language model can forecast such events after its training cutoff, rather than recall events before it. We rebuild a dated biomedical knowledge graph as it stood at the end of each year from 2020 up to its newest version. We then ask six open language models, with and without this graph, which targets will enter a first trial for a disease the next year. Without retrieval, the models rank about as well as trial history, a count of each target's past trials in the same therapeutic area, also after their training cutoffs. Evidence dated before the decision adds at most a small gain, before or after the models' training cutoffs. The newest graph raises five of six models clearly above that baseline, but its paths usually include the answer: the pair's own trial, dated after the decision. Evaluations of target prioritisation should date both features and labels, with evidence from before the decision and outcomes after it.

Navigent: A Geometry-Grounded Agentic Framework for Vision Language Navigation
Navigent：一个面向视觉语言导航的几何锚定智能体框架
Xinyu Zhou, Weiren Cai, Yitong Chen, Shenghai Yuan, Zihang Mu, Boyu Ma, Jiahua Dong, Yanshuo Lu, Jiaqi Bai, Jianfei Yang
cs.AI
large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
Vision-and-Language Navigation (VLN) with general-purpose multimodal large language models (MLLMs) offers a flexible alternative to task-specific navigation policies, while reliable long-horizon execution remains challenging. Agents must track navigation progress, detect discrepancies between commanded and actual motion, and recognize when movement has passed relevant landmarks or entrances. We present Navigent, an agentic VLN framework built around a frozen MLLM and a Geometry-Grounded Execution Critic (GEC). GEC performs two complementary checks: action-to-motion consistency, which evaluates measured displacement against commanded movement, and motion-to-landmark consistency, which tracks agent-selected visual anchors and entrance candidates in world coordinates. Detected discrepancies interrupt the remaining action sequence and trigger reobservation, local adjustment, or node-based recovery. Historical visual memory supports progress tracking across extended routes. An offline self-improvement procedure further analyzes successful and failed training trajectories to refine navigation prompts and GEC logic while keeping model weights fixed. On the R2R-CE validation-unseen split (1,839 episodes) and RxR-CE validation-unseen split(3,669 episodes), Navigent achieves 84.0%/86.0% SR and 72.9%/69.1% SPL, respectively, demonstrating the value of geometry-grounded execution verification for reliable agentic navigation. 使用通用多模态大语言模型（MLLMs）的视觉与语言导航（VLN）为任务特定的导航策略提供了一种灵活的替代方案，但可靠的长时程执行仍然具有挑战性。智能体必须跟踪导航进度，检测指令运动与实际运动之间的差异，并识别运动何时已经经过相关地标或入口。我们提出 Navigent，一个围绕冻结的 MLLM 和几何锚定执行评判器（GEC）构建的智能体式 VLN 框架。GEC 执行两项互补检查：动作到运动一致性，即根据指令运动评估测得的位移；以及运动到地标一致性，即在世界坐标中跟踪智能体选择的视觉锚点和入口候选。检测到的差异会中断剩余动作序列，并触发重新观察、局部调整或基于节点的恢复。历史视觉记忆支持在较长路线上的进度跟踪。一个离线自改进过程进一步分析成功和失败的训练轨迹，以在保持模型权重固定的同时改进导航提示和 GEC 逻辑。在 R2R-CE 验证未见划分（1,839 个回合）和 RxR-CE 验证未见划分（3,669 个回合）上，Navigent 分别达到 84.0%/86.0% 的 SR 和 72.9%/69.1% 的 SPL，展示了几何锚定执行验证对于可靠智能体导航的价值。项目页面：https://marslab-navigent.github.io/navigent.github.io/ 代码：https://github.com/MarsLab-Navigent/Navigent

cs.AI / 16 / 2611.34250
MedSkill-E$^{2}$: Evaluating and Evolving Skills for Medical Agents
MedSkill-E$^{2}$：评估与演化医学智能体的技能
Jingjing Hua, Shaocong Wei, Jianghan Shen, Junzhi Ning, Min Cen, Cheng Tang, Ziyan Huang, Jiepeng Li, Fengshuo Liu, Kangkun Mao, Mouxiao Bian, Yirong Chen, Ming Hu, Jiyao Liu
cs.AI · cs.CL
large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
Large language model (LLM) agents increasingly use skills to access domain knowledge and complete real-world tasks. We observe that even when a skill specifies the rules and procedures needed for a task, agents may fail to apply them effectively during autonomous execution, a phenomenon we call skill Enable But Underuse (EBU). This issue is particularly consequential in medical tasks, where overlooking a single critical constraint can yield a plausible but incorrect result. To evaluate and address EBU, we introduce MedSkill-E$^{2}$, a framework for evaluating and evolving skills for medical agents. We construct EBU-Bench, a challenging benchmark covering 12 medically relevant task groups and associated skills, to evaluate agents' ability to use available skills autonomously. We quantify the EBU gap as the difference in skill-use accuracy between autonomous use and explicitly guided reading and application of the same skill. On EBU-Bench, all evaluated model-harness combinations exhibit EBU, with a mean gap of 43.94 percentage points (pp). For the same model, skill-use accuracy under autonomous use differs by up to 38.96 pp across harnesses. Motivated by these observations, we propose EBU-Evolve, which uses execution feedback from autonomous and explicitly guided skill use to distill effective guidance into reusable skill instructions. Relative to their pre-evolution versions, the revised skills improve skill-use accuracy during autonomous execution by 33.33 to 55.17 pp and continue to yield improvements when transferred across multiple models and harnesses. Our results show that autonomous skill-use accuracy varies across harnesses with the model and skill held fixed, and model rankings can change. EBU can persist even after a skill is opened. EBU-Evolve improves autonomous skill-use accuracy on unseen tasks within the same skill, with gains transferring across models and harnesses.
Chinese Translation
大语言模型（LLM）智能体越来越多地使用技能来获取领域知识并完成现实世界任务。我们观察到，即使一项技能规定了任务所需的规则和流程，智能体在自主执行过程中也可能无法有效应用它们，我们将这一现象称为技能启用但未充分使用（skill Enable But Underuse，EBU）。这一问题在医学任务中尤为关键，因为忽略单一关键约束就可能产生看似合理但错误的结果。为评估并解决 EBU，我们提出 MedSkill-E$^{2}$，一个用于评估和演化医学智能体技能的框架。我们构建了 EBU-Bench，一个具有挑战性的基准，涵盖 12 个医学相关任务组及相关技能，用于评估智能体自主使用可用技能的能力。我们将 EBU 差距量化为同一技能在自主使用与在明确指导下阅读和应用之间的技能使用准确率差异。在 EBU-Bench 上，所有被评估的模型-执行框架组合都表现出 EBU，平均差距为 43.94 个百分点（pp）。对于同一模型，自主使用下的技能使用准确率在不同执行框架之间最多相差 38.96 个百分点。受这些观察启发，我们提出 EBU-Evolve，它利用自主技能使用和明确指导下的技能使用所产生的执行反馈，将有效指导提炼为可复用的技能指令。相对于演化前版本，修订后的技能在自主执行期间将技能使用准确率提高 33.33 至 55.17 个百分点，并且在跨多个模型和执行框架迁移时继续带来提升。我们的结果表明，在模型和技能固定的情况下，自主技能使用准确率会随执行框架不同而变化，并且模型排名可能发生变化。即使技能已被打开，EBU 仍可能持续存在。EBU-Evolve 提高了同一技能内未见任务上的自主技能使用准确率，且增益可跨模型和执行框架迁移。

cs.AI / 17 / 2611.34254
Crucible: Evaluating LLM Agents in Executable Chemistry Research Environments
Crucible：在可执行化学研究环境中评估LLM智能体
Yinjun Liu, Xinye Li, Ruisen Peng, Lang Gao, Zixiang Xu, Zirui Song, Xiuying Chen
cs.AI
large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
Large language models (LLMs) perform well on chemistry knowledge benchmarks, which mainly assess question answering and isolated tasks. Chemical research, however, requires using specialized tools and interpreting their outputs to obtain chemically valid results. To address this gap, we introduce Crucible Bench to evaluate this ability across all four stages of the design-make-test-analyze (DMTA) cycle. The benchmark contains 1,078 tasks in 12 task families curated from 18 published datasets, covering molecular design, synthesis planning, experimental execution, closed-loop optimization, simulation, and analytical characterization. Agents access 75 domain-specific tools through the Model Context Protocol in seven isolated environments. Sandboxed graders verify the resulting synthesis routes, experimental protocols, and other outputs. Laboratory tasks use robotic simulators or previously measured experimental data. We evaluate 14 LLMs as agents and find that the best achieves an overall score of 0.545, with synthesis planning and closed-loop optimization emerging as the hardest domains. Overall performance does not predict optimization performance well: the model ranked twelfth overall achieves the highest score in closed-loop optimization. Error analysis also shows that agents often submit chemically invalid results despite running their tools successfully. Stronger models benefit more from tool access, but reliable use of chemical software remains a challenge that Crucible Bench can track as models improve.

大语言模型（LLMs）在化学知识基准上表现良好，这些基准主要评估问答和孤立任务。然而，化学研究需要使用专门工具并解释其输出，以获得化学上有效的结果。为弥补这一差距，我们引入 Crucible Bench，以评估设计-制备-测试-分析（DMTA）循环所有四个阶段的这一能力。该基准包含1,078个任务，分属12个任务家族，这些任务家族由18个已发表数据集整理而成，涵盖分子设计、合成规划、实验执行、闭环优化、模拟和分析表征。智能体在七个隔离环境中通过模型上下文协议访问75个领域特定工具。沙盒化评分器验证生成的合成路线、实验方案和其他输出。实验室任务使用机器人模拟器或先前测量的实验数据。我们将14个LLM作为智能体进行评估，发现最佳者取得0.545的总分，其中合成规划和闭环优化成为最难的领域。总体性能不能很好地预测优化性能：总体排名第十二的模型在闭环优化中取得最高分。错误分析还表明，智能体尽管成功运行了其工具，却常常提交化学上无效的结果。更强的模型从工具访问中获益更多，但可靠地使用化学软件仍然是一个挑战，而 Crucible Bench 可以在模型改进过程中跟踪这一挑战。

MeterRouter: Budget-Aware Dynamic Routing for Multi-Agent Systems
MeterRouter：面向多智能体系统的预算感知动态路由
Yue Xu, Leikun Yin, Ruiming Min, Yufeng Lai, Justin Andrew Johnson, Sitao Luan, Xiaotong Shen
cs.AI · cs.MA
large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
Multi-agent systems (MAS) built on large language models (LLMs) outperform single-agent systems, but inter-agent communication incurs substantial token overhead. While assigning a large LLM to every agent is common, it results in inefficient resource utilization, leaving the system far from the Pareto frontier. The cost of answering a query is set jointly by how many agents are recruited, the role and LLM assigned to each, and communication topology among them. Most existing routers treat cost only implicitly rather than as an explicit optimization constraint. A fixed accuracy-cost preference also cannot express how much a caller is willing to pay for a particular query. We introduce MeterRouter, a budget-aware dynamic router that incrementally synthesizes a collaboration graph by selecting each agent's role, LLM, incoming connections, and termination conditioned on the query and a per-query monetary budget. We initialize the router by imitating successful execution graphs, then jointly refine its decisions with a variant of Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) whose reward favors correct answers and penalizes spending and budget overruns. Across five benchmarks and a three-tier LLM pool, MeterRouter is (1) accurate, achieving performance comparable to the strongest MAS; (2) economical, reaching that accuracy at 82% lower cost than the strongest MAS router and extending the accuracy-cost frontier beyond the ceiling of single-agent systems; and (3) controllable, adapting its spending to the specified budget while rarely exceeding it.
Chinese Translation
基于大语言模型（LLM）构建的多智能体系统（MAS）优于单智能体系统，但智能体间的通信会带来大量的 token 开销。尽管为每个智能体分配一个大语言模型很常见，但这会导致资源利用效率低下，使系统远离帕累托前沿。回答一个查询的成本由招募多少智能体、分配给每个智能体的角色和 LLM，以及它们之间的通信拓扑共同决定。大多数现有路由器仅隐式地处理成本，而不是将其作为显式的优化约束。固定的准确率-成本偏好也无法表达调用方愿意为某个特定查询支付多少。我们提出 MeterRouter，一种预算感知的动态路由器，它以查询和每个查询的货币预算为条件，通过选择每个智能体的角色、LLM、传入连接和终止来增量式地合成协作图。我们通过模仿成功的执行图来初始化该路由器，然后使用一种 Group Relative Policy Optimization（GRPO）的变体联合优化其决策，该变体的奖励偏向正确答案，并对花费和预算超支进行惩罚。在五个基准测试和一个三层 LLM 池上，MeterRouter 具有以下特点：(1) 准确，达到与最强 MAS 相当的性能；(2) 经济，以比最强 MAS 路由器低 82% 的成本达到该准确率，并将准确率-成本前沿扩展到单智能体系统的上限之外；(3) 可控，能够使其支出适应指定预算，同时很少超出预算。

cs.AI / 19 / 2611.34400
EvoLink-Bench: A Benchmark for Evaluating Self-Evolving Agents in Long-Horizon Interdependent Task Streams
EvoLink-Bench：评估长时程相互依赖任务流中自演化智能体的基准
Wei Chen, Xiaodong Lu, Weihao Shen, Gongxun Li, Xingyu Guo, Qihang Sun, Fuwei Zhang, Zhao Zhang, Yikun Ban, Shuang Li, Deqing Wang, Fuzhen Zhuang
cs.AI
large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
Large language model (LLM) agents are evolving from passive chatbots into autonomous systems that operate continuously in dynamic environments. Such agents need not only solve current tasks but also learn from past interactions to improve future performance. However, existing streaming benchmarks often rely on short task sequences or largely independent tasks, providing limited evidence of whether agents can effectively reuse experience when later tasks depend on earlier outcomes. To address this gap, we introduce \textbf{EvoLink-Bench}, a benchmark for evaluating self-evolving agents in long-horizon, interdependent task streams. It covers daily office work, multi-turn dialogue, and AutoResearch-style workflows, with persistent workspaces and dependencies across tasks. The benchmark includes two complementary levels: \textbf{L1}, which evaluates the acquisition and revision of language-expressible knowledge, and \textbf{L2}, which assesses the development of task-level capabilities through execution and feedback. Its evaluation further distinguishes within-task recovery, persistent-state updates, and experience reuse in later tasks. We evaluate five agent frameworks across three backbone configurations under three persistence conditions, covering 19,635 scored task slots from selected evaluation cohorts. Results show that no framework consistently performs best across both levels, retries recover only a limited proportion of failed tasks, and persistent-state updates do not necessarily improve subsequent performance. Furthermore, the effects of evolution differ between knowledge- and capability-level tasks, suggesting that these two forms of evolution require different learning mechanisms. Performance gains also vary across domains and task streams, with improvements on some tasks not necessarily extending to others.

大型语言模型（LLM）智能体正在从被动的聊天机器人演化为能够在动态环境中持续运行的自主系统。此类智能体不仅需要解决当前任务，还需要从过去的交互中学习，以提升未来表现。然而，现有的流式基准往往依赖短任务序列或基本相互独立的任务，对于当后续任务依赖先前结果时智能体能否有效复用经验，提供的证据有限。为弥合这一空白，我们引入 \textbf{EvoLink-Bench}，一个用于评估长时程、相互依赖任务流中自演化智能体的基准。它涵盖日常办公工作、多轮对话和 AutoResearch 风格的工作流，并具有持久工作区以及跨任务的依赖关系。该基准包括两个互补层次：\textbf{L1} 评估可用语言表达的知识的获取与修正，\textbf{L2} 通过执行与反馈评估任务级能力的发展。其评估进一步区分任务内恢复、持久状态更新以及后续任务中的经验复用。我们在三种持久化条件下、跨三种骨干配置评估了五种智能体框架，覆盖来自选定评估队列的 19,635 个已评分任务槽。结果表明，没有框架在两个层次上始终表现最佳，重试仅能恢复有限比例的失败任务，并且持久状态更新未必能改善后续表现。此外，演化效应在知识级任务与能力级任务之间存在差异，这表明这两种演化形式需要不同的学习机制。性能增益也因领域和任务流而异，某些任务上的改进未必能迁移到其他任务。

cs.AI / 20 / 2611.34440
vSFT: Learning to Verbally Tune Agents at Test Time
vSFT：学习在测试时通过语言调优智能体
Qishuai Wen, Rui Chen, Haiwen Li, Zhiyuan Huang, Qiwen Gu, Bingjie Gao, Geng Li, Jing Tang, Xiangxiang Chu, Chun-Guang Li
cs.AI · cs.CL · cs.LG
large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
Large language model agents are increasingly improved via agentic reinforcement learning, which can be on-policy but suffers from expensive rollouts and sparse rewards, limiting its application at test time. In this paper, we present a verbally Supervised Fine-Tuning (vSFT) framework that enables the conjunction of dense feedback in natural language and weight updates at test time. Specifically, our vSFT forms a closed loop between an agent and a supervisor via a hypernetwork, in which the supervisor generates verbal supervision from the agent's failed trajectories, and the hypernetwork converts that supervision into low-rank weight updates to tune the agent. We validate that this test-time in-parameter evolving process outperforms both its in-context counterparts and prevalent reinforcement learning methods. In particular, our vSFT using Qwen3-4B outperforms GRPO and Reflexion by 8.7% and 13.9% in success rate on ALFWorld, and by 4.8% and 18.2% on WebShop, respectively. We believe that learning how to adapt a model, rather than an adapted model, offers a promising path towards more capable agents that improve themselves.
Chinese Translation
大语言模型智能体正越来越多地通过智能体强化学习得到改进；这类方法可以是同策略的，但受制于昂贵的 rollout 和稀疏奖励，从而限制了其在测试时的应用。本文提出一种言语监督微调（vSFT）框架，该框架能够在测试时将自然语言中的稠密反馈与权重更新结合起来。具体而言，我们的 vSFT 通过一个超网络在智能体与监督者之间形成闭环，其中监督者根据智能体的失败轨迹生成言语监督，而超网络将该监督转换为低秩权重更新以调优智能体。我们验证了这种测试时的参数内演化过程优于其上下文内对应方法以及主流的强化学习方法。特别地，使用 Qwen3-4B 的我们的 vSFT 在 ALFWorld 上的成功率分别比 GRPO 和 Reflexion 高出 8.7% 和 13.9%，在 WebShop 上分别高出 4.8% 和 18.2%。我们认为，学习如何适配一个模型，而不是学习一个已适配的模型，为通向能够自我改进的更强智能体提供了一条有前景的路径。

cs.AI / 21 / 2611.34635
ZeroHero: Training Small Language Agents from Scratch
ZeroHero：从头训练小型语言智能体
Nikita Sorokin, Zoya Volovikova, Alexey Skrynnik, Aleksandr Panov
cs.AI
large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
Large pretrained language models provide capable policies for interactive tasks, but how much model capacity is necessary for a specialized language agent? We introduce ZeroHero, a framework for training small language agents (SLAs) from scratch. In each environment, a large language model acts as the expert, and we collect its successful trajectories. We pretrain each SLA, which has fewer than 50 million parameters, to predict the expert's responses given the interaction history. We then post-train the agent on its own interactions using proximal policy optimization (PPO). During post-training, reasoning alignment supplements environment rewards with expert supervision on the language the agent generates alongside its actions. We evaluate the agents in three multistep environments where acting requires both understanding and generating language. In Crafter, agents interpret textual observations and generate reasoning before acting. In WebShop, they translate shopping instructions into search queries. In Alfworld-Dialogue, they ask clarifying questions and use the answers to guide household actions. The agents approach expert performance on WebShop and surpass their respective demonstration experts on Crafter training rollouts and held-out Alfworld-Dialogue tasks. An interactive demo is available at https://zoyav.github.io/-ZoyaV-zerohero-demo.
Chinese Translation
大型预训练语言模型为交互任务提供了能力强大的策略，但对于一个专门化的语言智能体而言，多少模型容量是必要的？我们提出 ZeroHero，一个从头训练小型语言智能体（SLA）的框架。在每个环境中，大型语言模型充当专家，我们收集其成功的轨迹。我们预训练每个 SLA（其参数量少于 5000 万），使其在给定交互历史的情况下预测专家的响应。然后，我们使用近端策略优化（PPO）在智能体自身的交互上对其进行后训练。在后训练期间，推理对齐通过专家对智能体在行动同时所生成语言的监督，来补充环境奖励。我们在三个多步环境中评估这些智能体，在这些环境中，行动既需要理解语言，也需要生成语言。在 Crafter 中，智能体解释文本观测，并在行动前生成推理。在 WebShop 中，它们将购物指令转换为搜索查询。在 Alfworld-Dialogue 中，它们提出澄清性问题，并利用答案来指导家务行动。这些智能体在 WebShop 上接近专家性能，并在 Crafter 训练推演和留出的 Alfworld-Dialogue 任务上超越各自对应的示范专家。交互式演示可在 https://zoyav.github.io/-ZoyaV-zerohero-demo 获取。

cs.AI / 22 / 2611.34751
What Is a Theory Worth to an LLM Solver? Measuring, Inducing, and Merging Theories in Context
理论对 LLM 求解器有多大价值？在上下文中度量、诱导与合并理论
Jun Gao, Shuchao Bi
cs.AI
large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
Mathematicians solve problems faster when they know the right theory. We ask how much a stated theory is worth to a large language model (LLM) solver, and whether a model can write that theory itself. In a length-matched protocol, adding the right theory to the context of Qwen3-14B raises pass@1 on pattern waiting-time problems from 0.37 to 0.83 and cuts the median tokens of correct solutions from 10.2k to 6.3k, while worked examples of the same length do not help. The gain shrinks as the solver and its token budget grow (+0.46, +0.26, +0.07), and at a long budget it comes almost entirely from finishing within budget: solutions that finish are correct 98--100\% of the time in every condition. To separate induction from recall, we plant unpublished theorems in custom probability families and measure how much of the oracle theory's gain an induced theory recovers. A strong open model, required to explore the training problems with code before writing, recovers 60\% of the gain on one planted family, 48\% on a second, and almost none on a third, where it finds the right form but not the condition that makes the form computable. No single induced note is complete, but a strong model that merges several notes recovers 61\% of the gain on the classic family, above the best single note (47\%). Theories are worth the reasoning they save, and models can find their pieces before they can assemble them.

Knowledge-Base Gradient Descent: Self-Structuring Learning through Question Answering

Masahiro Kato
cs.AI · cs.LG
large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
We consider the problem of constructing knowledge bases for applications based on large language models, in which the structure of a knowledge base determines how an application can retrieve and connect the information needed to answer a question. We study Self-Structuring Learning, a setting in which questions and expected answers guide the construction of a persistent knowledge base whose editable structure can be a graph schema or the organization of linked knowledge documents. We propose Knowledge-Base Gradient Descent, which diagnoses discrepancies between expected answers and responses obtained through the current knowledge base. At each round, the method proposes a structural edit, rebuilds the knowledge base, and adopts the edit when the learning loss decreases. The retained structure is evaluated on other questions about the same sources. By randomizing over candidate edits, we express the loss change of an edit as a derivative with respect to the probability of selecting it, and we evaluate joint edits as single candidates because their changes interact. Schema Descent instantiates the method for graph schemas. In experiments on large documents, each a bundle of research papers, the updated knowledge cards and graph schemas obtain higher mean Answer F1 on held-out generated questions than their initial structures, with schema gains in every document. On human questions, mean F1 rises for schemas and falls for cards: the updated structures serve the kind of question they were learned from.

NEVA: Natural-Language Co-Evolution and Validation of Microarchitectures

Khoi Le, Sayanti Jana, Matthew DeLorenzo, Jeyavijayan Rajendran, Paul Gratz
cs.AR
large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
Recent large language model (LLM)-guided evolutionary approaches have demonstrated the potential to automate microarchitectural design exploration. However, existing approaches primarily evolve C++ simulator code rather than reasoning directly about the microarchitectural designs it represents. As C++ code embodies hardware designs with several layers of abstraction, evolving it directly forces LLMs to reason through implementation details rather than the actual architectural mechanisms, hardware state, and decision rules that define a microarchitectural design. To this end, we propose NEVA, an LLM-guided methodology that generates new microarchitectural policies by extracting, integrating and adapting architectural concepts from published research. NEVA extracts the underlying concepts from prior works into a structured knowledge library, which then guides the evolution of joint natural-language architectural specifications. This approach addresses three key challenges: architectural representation in natural language, validation of candidate designs under hardware constraints, and the coordination of microarchitecture components using diagnostic feedback through co-evolution. We evaluate NEVA across single-core and multicore configurations using SPEC CPU2017/2026, Google, GAP, and XSBench workloads, and compare specification-level evolution against code-level evolution across different search strategies. Under Claude Opus 5.5, NEVA discovers designs achieving up to 4.8% higher held-out single-core performance than the Pythia-Mockingjay baseline. A selected EvoX design achieves improvements of 3.4% and 1.5% under full and restricted memory bandwidth, respectively, although its multicore performance does not differ significantly from the baseline. The EvoX search evaluates 40 candidates over 2.2 days, with approximately $320 in LLM usage at API list prices.

A Differential Computing Accelerator for LLM Inference Leveraging Bit-Slice Transition Sparsity
一种利用位切片转移稀疏性的LLM推理差分计算加速器
Yifan Wang, Zetao Guo, You Xiao, Wendi Sun, Song Chen
cs.AR
large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
Large language models (LLMs) have become foundational to modern artificial intelligence. Driven by scaling laws, their rapid growth poses increasing computational and memory challenges for deployment. To accelerate the general matrix multiplication (GEMM) operations that dominate LLM computation, bit-slice architectures decompose quantized operands along the bit dimension, exposing slice-level sparsity and redundancy. However, existing bit-slice designs primarily exploit sparsity in high-order slices, while dense low-order slices still offer substantial untapped reuse opportunities. We observe that bit-slice vectors (BSVs) are highly clustered in Hamming space, with many BSVs lying only a few bit flips away from a small set of representative patterns. Based on this observation, we propose ISTS, an algorithm-hardware co-designed accelerator that leverages representative BSV patterns as shared Steiner points to reuse partial sums across slices, substantially reducing computation. Specifically, the partial sum of each target BSV can be reconstructed from that of its assigned Steiner point using only a few additions or subtractions. On the algorithmic side, we propose Steiner Absorption Table Construction (SATC), which selects a compact set of Steiner points to absorb BSVs with only a few bidirectional bit flips, while FlipPrune selectively prunes flips to further expand the reusable BSV population. On the hardware side, we design a lightweight accelerator that supports Steiner reuse for static linear layer weights and runtime-generated attention K/V tensors. Comprehensive evaluations show that ISTS achieves average speedups of $3.09\times$, $2.41\times$, $2.18\times$, $1.27\times$, and $1.41\times$ over the state-of-the-art accelerators ANT, BBS, LUT Tensor Core, Transitive Array, and MCBP-BRCR, respectively.

Evaluating Large Language Models on conversational African American English: Feature classification and next-turn generation
在对话式非裔美国人英语上评估大型语言模型：特征分类与下一轮生成
Romeo De Timmerman, Thomas Demeester, Els Lefever
cs.CL
large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
Large Language Models (LLMs) are known to misinterpret and misrepresent regional and social varieties of English other than Mainstream American English (MAE), such as African American English (AAE), yet most evaluations of these biases have relied on synthetic, stylized or decontextualized data. This paper instead evaluates LLMs on authentic, conversational AAE to more closely reflect how such models may encounter AAE when deployed as chatbots. Concretely, we perform two complementary evaluation tasks on 100 six-turn segments randomly sampled from the Corpus of Regional African American Language (CORAAL; Kendall and Farrington, 2024), comparing three closed-weight LLM configurations: Gemini 2.5 Flash with and without reasoning, and GPT-4.1 mini. The first task compares the models against gold-standard manual annotations for five AAE morphosyntactic features, while the second assesses their ability to generate contextually appropriate next turns, evaluating outputs for AAE feature frequency, diversity (Self-BLEU), and pragmatic quality. Reasoning-enabled Gemini is the strongest feature detector by a clear margin (macro F1 of 0.91), outperforming both other LLMs as well as a finetuned BERT-based baseline (Masis et al., 2022). In generation, however, all LLMs underproduce AAE relative to the human speakers and produce relatively uniform continuations, with reasoning-enabled Gemini producing the least AAE and the least diverse output. We conclude that a model's ability to detect AAE does not straightforwardly translate into its spontaneous use of AAE in generation, and argue that addressing this gap requires changes upstream, in how pretraining and alignment data represent dialectal variation.

Failure Broadens, Success Sharpens: Continual Adaptation of Tool-Use Agents Across Diverse Tasks with Dual-Polarity Memory
失败拓宽，成功锐化：双极性记忆下工具使用智能体跨多样任务的持续适应
Tianmai M. Zhang, Hoda Shajari, Amr Hendy, Xiaohu Liu, Piyush Behre, Omar Zia Khan, Ankur Gupta
cs.CL
large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
Large language model agents can self-improve over time by utilizing procedural memory derived from prior task trajectories, yet the distinct utilities of memories derived from local successes and failures remain underexplored. This work studies this question in a realistic setting with heterogeneous streams of multi-domain tool-use tasks and various environment constraints common in real-world scenarios. We develop \emph{Dual-Polarity Memory with Periodic Maintenance} (DualPM), a simple, retrieval-free memory workflow characterized by (1) customizable reflection and procedural memory generation from both local successes and failures within each trajectory, and (2) periodic memory consolidation over long task streams under a given memory capacity, preventing memory explosion. Online prequential evaluation with fine-grained metrics reveals that failure memory more strongly broadens coverage, success memory better streamlines execution, while combining both polarities effectively integrates both benefits. Further studies demonstrate that DualPM enables cross-domain memory generalization and continual memory adaptation, while external evaluation on EvoMemBench reveals the portability and effectiveness of DualPM as a general long-term procedural memory method.

Verifiable but Not Predictable: What Sentence Embeddings Know About Propositional Decomposition
可验证但不可预测：句子嵌入关于命题分解知道什么
Qingan Li, Tianxiao Wu, Xiling Cui
cs.CL · cs.LG
large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
Quality control for proposition decomposition by large language models (LLMs) raises two asymmetric questions. After decomposition, one can verify: given a sentence and a candidate proposition, does the proposition belong to that sentence? Before decomposition, one would like to predict: how many propositions should the sentence yield? On PropSegmEnt, a corpus of English Wikipedia sentences each segmented by three human annotators, we find that the two questions live in different representational spaces. A natural language inference (NLI) judge verifies membership with 92.8% accuracy and an area under the ROC curve (AUC) of 0.977, and its residual errors turn out to be mostly propositions that are true in document context rather than genuine entailment mistakes. Vector geometry cannot verify: cosine similarity saturates, and a sentence embedding is not a linear combination of its propositions' embeddings. For prediction, every symbolic anchor we test, namely token count, the CPIDR idea-density counter, and a Neo-Davidsonian predicate count, reduces to a length proxy once token count is controlled. A linear ridge probe on sentence embeddings is the only predictor that keeps genuine count signal: its length-partialled correlation with human counts is 0.40-0.49 with bootstrap confidence intervals (CIs) excluding zero, and it orders length-matched sentence pairs correctly 67-71% of the time against a 50% chance level, statistically matching the inter-annotator agreement ceiling. This signal survives INT8 quantization without loss, INT4 at a small cost, and Matryoshka truncation to 256 dimensions, and it works as well in a 2021 encoder as in a 2025 one. Its structured weakness is a systematic under-splitting of long sentences. We distill the protocol lessons, including a retracted pilot study, into a checklist for probing length-confounded quantities.

Rethinking Knowledge Distillation for Diffusion Language Models
重新审视扩散语言模型的知识蒸馏
Yuxuan Sun, Yuanjian Xu, Jianing Hao, Yu Li, Sowmen Das, Zhong Li, Sangwoong Yoon, Miguel R. D. Rodrigues
cs.CL
diffusion
扩散模型相关
Abstract
Knowledge distillation has recently proven highly effective for improving autoregressive models, but its applicability to DLMs remains poorly understood. We present the first systematic study of KD for DLMs and uncover two non-intuitive failures of classical forward-KL (FKL) distillation: (i) student perplexity does not improve monotonically with more teacher-generated data, and (ii) on the same teacher-generated corpus, FKL distillation underperforms simply training the student with the original DLM denoising objective. To address them, we propose a unified, data-free distillation framework for masked DLMs. First, the framework runs an off-policy distillation phase that absorbs general knowledge from a static set of teacher-generated data. Then, the framework employs on-policy distillation which consists of three techniques: a trajectory loss along the student's own reverse process, confidence reweighting that down-weights tokens where the teacher is unsure, and a trust-region anchor that stabilizes the moving target. On MDLM, the resulting student attains a GPT-2 perplexity of $24.75$, surpassing the teacher's $27.04$; on Dream-7B distillation to a 93M student model, the framework reduces Qwen-2.5 perplexity from the FKL-distilled baseline of $25.23$ to $19.83$ while preserving performance on zero-shot general capability benchmarks.

Rethinking Sequential Locate-Then-Edit: Optimality and Stability
重新审视序列式定位-编辑：最优性与稳定性
Bingqing Liu, Wei Liu, Zhiying Deng, Jun Wang, Yuhua Li, Ruixuan Li
cs.CL · cs.AI
large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
The Locate-Then-Edit framework enables efficient knowledge updates in large language models without requiring full retraining. Recent research has increasingly focused on sequential editing, where knowledge arrives continuously and the model is updated incrementally. However, existing sequential methods commonly suffer from catastrophic forgetting and model collapse after only a few hundred edits. In contrast, batch editing - which jointly optimizes all edits and yields the optimal solution under a specified editing objective - can support tens of thousands of edits with high edit efficacy while preserving the model's general capabilities, resulting in a substantial performance gap between the two editing paradigms. In this paper, we demonstrate that this gap can be closed via a batch-equivalent sequential editing approach. Moreover, we investigate the underlying mechanism of model degradation in existing sequential methods by analyzing the convergence behavior of weight perturbations as edits accumulate. Our analysis reveals that current methods typically exhibit linear or logarithmic growth in perturbation, whereas the proposed batch-equivalent method achieves time-invariant growth, thereby theoretically guaranteeing long-term stability and preserving the integrity of pretrained knowledge throughout massive-scale sequential editing.

定位-编辑框架能够在不需完整重新训练的情况下实现大语言模型中的高效知识更新。近期研究越来越关注序列编辑，其中知识持续到来，模型被增量更新。然而，现有序列方法通常仅在几百次编辑后就遭受灾难性遗忘和模型崩溃。相比之下，批量编辑——它联合优化所有编辑，并在指定编辑目标下产生最优解——能够以高编辑有效性支持数万次编辑，同时保持模型的通用能力，从而导致两种编辑范式之间存在显著性能差距。本文表明，这一差距可以通过一种批量等效的序列编辑方法来弥合。此外，我们通过分析随着编辑累积权重扰动的收敛行为，研究现有序列方法中模型退化的潜在机制。我们的分析揭示，当前方法通常表现出扰动的线性或对数增长，而所提出的批量等效方法实现了时不变增长，从而在理论上保证长期稳定性，并在大规模序列编辑过程中保持预训练知识的完整性。

NORMCRAFT: Cultural Norm Generation for Context-Aware Language Model Alignment

Tangyuan Zhang, Zhuang Li, Fatemeh Shiri, Xiangyu Zhao, Junyu Yan, Xiuzhen Zhang
cs.CL
large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
Cultural alignment requires large language models (LLMs) to infer often-implicit social norms from a scenario and its cultural context. Existing approaches typically adapt individual models or supply external cultural knowledge, while learning norm inference independently of downstream response generation remains underexplored. We introduce NORMCRAFT, a modular framework that decouples norm inference from response generation. Through norm-centric multi-view supervision, we train an LLM as a norm generator to recover shared norms from prospective, adherence, and violation scenarios without downstream response labels. The generated norms guide a separate, frozen LLM (the responder). With Qwen3.5-4B as the responder, NORMCRAFT outperforms prompting and supervised fine-tuning (SFT) baselines on four of five downstream metrics. On SafeWorld, its responses reflect the reference norms more often (Coverage) and more precisely (Faithfulness), exceeding Responder SFT by 18.0 and 14.1 percentage points, respectively. Direct norm evaluation also shows higher norm quality than the base and few-shot generators. The same trained generator improves cultural alignment on SafeWorld across fourteen frozen LLMs spanning five families and 0.8B to 27B parameters, with the largest gains for the smallest models.

Pitfalls of Dependency-Ready Decoding for Masked Diffusion Language Models
掩码扩散语言模型的依赖就绪解码的隐患
Lina Berrayana, Christopher Malon, Yoichi Ishibashi, Taichi Aida, Masafumi Oyamada
cs.CL · cs.AI · cs.LG
diffusion
扩散模型相关
Abstract
Masked diffusion models (MDMs) have shown strong performance on structured reasoning tasks such as Sudoku, Trip Planning, and Countdown. MDMs introduce a freedom in the order in which tokens may be unmasked, and to exercise this freedom for good accuracy, early decoding strategies relied on signals of confidence or the downstream impact of decoding a token. However, simple examples seem to illustrate that resolving a token's dependencies before unmasking it should be important. Therefore, we examine whether this principle, which we call dependency-ready decoding, would contribute to better accuracy, from a practical and a theoretical perspective. We examine a recent decoder that implements dependency-readiness through attention, and generally find that when it performs better than confidence-based or future utility baselines, its decoding order collapses to left-to-right decoding. For theoretical analysis, we establish a definition of dependency without resorting to attention, measured by an information-theoretic score of how much revealing a single masked token (or a set) would shift the model's prediction for another. We prove that when the margin is large relative to this score, no such revelation can change the top prediction, so in this regime Maximum-Margin decoding already commits dependency-ready tokens. These findings leave only a narrow scope for future dependency-ready decoders: their potential benefit is limited to positions with margins smaller than the information-theoretic sensitivity, and reliance on attention should be questioned.
Chinese Translation
掩码扩散模型（MDMs）在诸如数独（Sudoku）、旅行规划（Trip Planning）和倒计时（Countdown）等结构化推理任务上已展现出强劲性能。MDMs 引入了 token 可以被解除掩码的顺序上的自由度，而为了利用这一自由度获得良好准确率，早期的解码策略依赖于置信度信号或解码某个 token 的下游影响。然而，简单的例子似乎表明，在解除某个 token 的掩码之前先解决其依赖关系应当是重要的。因此，我们从实践和理论两个视角考察这一我们称之为依赖就绪解码的原则是否会带来更好的准确率。我们考察了一个通过注意力机制实现依赖就绪性的近期解码器，并普遍发现，当它比基于置信度或未来效用的基线表现更好时，其解码顺序会退化为从左到右解码。为进行理论分析，我们建立了一个不借助注意力机制的依赖性定义，该定义由一个信息论分数来度量，即揭示单个掩码 token（或一个集合）会在多大程度上改变模型对另一个 token 的预测。我们证明，当裕度相对于该分数较大时，任何这样的揭示都无法改变最高预测，因此在这一情形下，最大裕度解码已经提交了依赖就绪的 token。这些发现只为未来的依赖就绪解码器留下了狭窄的空间：其潜在收益仅限于裕度小于信息论敏感度的位置，并且对注意力机制的依赖应当受到质疑。

ChemDeduce: Benchmarking LLMs for Unknown Chemical Identification through Interactive Simulated Experiments
ChemDeduce：通过交互式模拟实验对 LLMs 进行未知化学物质识别的基准测试
Hengyi Cai, Yuqi Tang, Zichang Li, Huajun chen, Qiang Zhang, Keyan Ding
cs.CL · cs.LG
large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
Large language models (LLMs) have shown strong performance in chemical knowledge and reasoning, yet it remains unclear whether they can solve problems whose answers must be discovered through experimentation. We investigate this question through Unknown Chemical Identification, where a model must actively design experiments, interpret observations, update hypotheses, and ultimately identify a hidden substance. We introduce ChemDeduce, an interactive evaluation framework for assessing LLMs through simulated experiments. ChemDeduce formulates chemical identification as a sequential decision process and provides a stateful simulated laboratory with explicit instrument and operational constraints, enabling scalable and reproducible evaluation of iterative experimental reasoning. We benchmark eight frontier LLMs on 200 chemicals, yielding 1600 model--target pairs and 4800 episodes over three independent repetitions, and evaluate identification accuracy, operational compliance, interaction efficiency, and trajectory-level reasoning quality. Despite generating seemingly plausible experimental plans, current models achieve an average identification accuracy ranging from 23.83% to 67.33%, revealing substantial limitations in experiment selection, evidence interpretation, and sequential hypothesis refinement.

大型语言模型（LLMs）在化学知识与推理方面已表现出强劲性能，但它们能否解决那些必须通过实验才能发现答案的问题仍不清楚。我们通过未知化学物质识别（Unknown Chemical Identification）来研究这一问题，其中模型必须主动设计实验、解释观察结果、更新假设，并最终识别出一种隐藏物质。我们提出 ChemDeduce，一个通过模拟实验评估 LLMs 的交互式评测框架。ChemDeduce 将化学识别形式化为一个序列决策过程，并提供一个带有明确仪器约束和操作约束的有状态模拟实验室，从而能够对迭代式实验推理进行可扩展且可复现的评估。我们在 200 种化学物质上对八个前沿 LLMs 进行基准测试，在三次独立重复中得到 1600 个模型--目标对和 4800 个回合，并评估识别准确率、操作合规性、交互效率以及轨迹级推理质量。尽管当前模型生成了看似合理的实验计划，它们的平均识别准确率仅在 23.83% 到 67.33% 之间，暴露出在实验选择、证据解释和序列假设细化方面存在显著局限。

Contextual language representations link narrative processing to language and literacy in children
情境化语言表征将叙事加工与儿童的语言和读写能力联系起来
Dongyi He, Tian Jiang, Nizhuan Wang, Wai Ting Siok
cs.CL
large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
Spoken narratives extensively connect moment-to-moment language processing with knowledge accumulated through language and literacy experience. This study examined that relationship using functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) during Cantonese story listening and contextual representations from large language model (LLM). The imaging cohort comprised 23 school-age children; 16 contributed complete standardized literacy and language assessments and served as held-out participants in a nested cross-subject encoding analysis of the same story. Contextual embeddings predicted distributed narrative responses, with prominent correspondence in temporoparietal and default-network parcels. Regional summaries of the top 25% of voxels ranked by held-out correlation yielded atlas-wide means of r=0.174 and partial R2=0.0165. A joint feature model identified negative surprisal and positive predictive-entropy coefficients across cortical and subcortical parcels, including control, salience, hippocampal and amygdalar regions. Higher word-dictation and overall literacy scores were associated with lower regional encoding performance. Higher Cantonese grammar scores were associated with more negative semantic-update coefficients in parietal control, somatomotor and dorsal-attention parcels. Together, these findings connect language and literacy skills to the regional strength and direction of neural coupling with narrative context. They position naturalistic context processing as a possibly measurable link between oral comprehension and literacy in childhood.

DiCALM: Converting Autoregressive Convolution-Attention Language Models into Discrete Diffusion Language Models

Phong Le, Ngoc-Quan Pham, Dat Quoc Nguyen
cs.CL · cs.AI
diffusion
扩散模型相关
Abstract
Existing methods for adapting autoregressive (AR) language models to diffusion generation focus mainly on full-attention architectures. More efficient hybrid architectures remain underexplored. We introduce DiCALM, a recipe for converting the hybrid convolution-attention models of the LFM2 family (LFM2 and LFM2.5) from AR to masked-diffusion generation. DiCALM progressively extends LFM2's causal gated convolution so that it captures local context in both directions. It combines this extension with a masking warm-up and joint AR--diffusion training. In controlled experiments, DiCALM performs comparably to the corresponding fine-tuned LFM2.5-based AR models and delivers consistent speedups over them at both the 350M and 1.2B scales: over 1.4x on average and up to 1.79x.

Fine-Tuning Without Gradients? Closed-Form, LLM-Written Classifiers on a Frozen Encoder
无需梯度的微调？在冻结编码器上的闭式、由 LLM 编写的分类器
Md Nasir Uddin, Musa Tur Farazi, Soumik Bhattacharjee, Tishna Sabrina, Chowdhury Mohammad Rakin Haider
cs.CL · cs.AI · cs.LG
large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
Can a classifier computed in closed form on a frozen encoder match gradient fine-tuning? We present closed-form weight-space programming (WSP): a large language model (LLM), used as a design assistant, writes programs that read a frozen masked language model through cloze-style prompt templates at several layers, fit closed-form heads (shrinkage discriminant analysis, kernel ridge regression and the encoder's label-word prior) on labelled data, and select among a pool of candidate heads by cross-fitting. No gradient is computed and no encoder weight changes. We instantiate the framework on RoBERTa-large. On 11 development datasets with 512 to 8,192 training labels, WSP is ahead of full fine-tuning (FT) and LoRA at every label budget (by 0.3 to 0.6 points on average; the registered non-inferiority tests pass) and within 0.5 points of prompt-based fine-tuning (PFT); these datasets also shaped the recipe. With fewer labels its lead over FT and LoRA grows: 1.2 to 3.5 points with 64 and 128 labels, and 3.8 to 5.3 points in the few-shot setting of 16 labels per class, where WSP is again within half a point of PFT on the development datasets. On six held-out datasets, WSP stays ahead of LoRA and within half a point of FT on average, although with six datasets no registered test passes, and PFT is ahead, by 1.30 points with 8,192 labels. WSP never collapses and is deterministic, but it needs one encoder pass per template (17 here). We report all eight recipe versions, every decision that saw test results, and 27 ideas that did not help.

Dmytro Babarytskyi, Oleksandr Babarytskyi, Vadym Savanevych

large language model

Abstract
Organisations deploying large language models in Ukrainian-language information systems need to know whether a model produces normative Ukrainian. This paper establishes a protocol for measuring that reliably and applies it to 19 models. The instrument is a released set of 1,444 Ukrainian minimal pairs covering the vocative case, numeral-noun and adjective agreement, verb government and calques from russian, with subject-verb agreement as a control; a quarter of the set was checked against the answer key in two independent native-speaker ratings, which agreed at Cohen's $κ$ = 0.963. Every pair is scored twice: by comparing the probabilities a model assigns to the two sentences, and by asking the model directly, with the sentences presented in both orders so that answer-position effects are measured instead of being absorbed into the score. Three results follow. Order consistency (the share of pairs answered identically when the sentences are exchanged) falls below 0.05 for ten of the nineteen models, and what separates the usable models is instruction tuning, not scale. The vocative case is systematically inverted: 0.153 accuracy against 0.951 on the control, with models preferring the non-normative nominative form of address. Ukrainian adaptation substantially reduces this deficit, measured against the exact checkpoints two adapted models were trained from.

cs.CL
large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
Rubric-based benchmarks such as HealthBench evaluate large language models (LLMs) on open-ended health consultations using case-specific physician criteria, many of which presuppose the healthcare institutions, medications, and care pathways of their source region. Under machine translation alone, these regional assumptions remain in the rubric, leaving responses appropriate in Japan uncredited or falsely penalized under foreign clinical rules. To adapt established clinical evaluation perspectives to Japan without authoring rubrics from scratch, we construct JHealthBench-L (79 patient-facing consultations, 1,022 criteria) through source-cited LLM drafting, single-specialist selection and revision, independent dual-physician review, and meta-review. Specialists rewrote only 4.4% of criteria from scratch, and independent reviewers approved 93.6% of Stage-2 criteria without issue. Comparing JHealthBench-L with a machine-translated baseline across 18 LLMs reveals that translation-only evaluation preserves coarse model rankings ($τ= 0.817$, mean shift +0.027) yet flips verdicts on 17.7% of modified criteria (vs. 7.3% re-grading noise) and reduces false penalties on Japan-adapted negative criteria by 7.1 percentage points, masking item-level clinical mismeasurement behind stable leaderboards. Axis-level and paired analyses further show that context awareness and Japan-specific clinical criteria remain primary bottlenecks, whereas Japanese continual pretraining and reasoning post-training substantially improve locally grounded performance. Datasets, physician revision logs, and evaluation code are available at https://github.com/horshohei/JHealthBench-L.

Abstract
Legal due diligence in mergers and acquisitions requires lawyers to organize heterogeneous virtual data room documents, extract transaction-relevant information and consolidate reviewed findings into a due diligence report. We present LEXI (Legal Extraction and Intelligence), a work-in-progress system that demonstrates how large language models can support this process from document ingestion to report preparation. LEXI classifies documents under a configurable due diligence taxonomy, assigns relevant target entities, extracts predefined information with supporting passages and page-level provenance and prepares report content from reviewed findings. Structured outputs connect these stages and allow model-generated results to be passed through the workflow in a controlled form. Lawyers review and correct classifications and extractions and retain responsibility for legal assessments, recommendations, risk ratings and final report wording. Initial evaluations of the classification and extraction components provide preliminary evidence that the approach is feasible. Lightweight Reasoning Transfer via Chain-of-Thought Vector Projection
通过思维链向量投影的轻量级推理迁移
Yulin Qi, Shuo Xu, Shuxia Lin, Qingjian Ni, Xu Yang, Xin Geng
cs.CL
large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
Transferring reasoning capabilities from large language models to smaller ones often requires extensive teacher supervision or costly student adaptation. We study projected cross-model Chain-of-Thought (CoT) Vector transfer, a two-stage approach that keeps both models frozen. First, we learn a task-level CoT Vector in the teacher using dataset-provided solution traces and final-answer supervision. We then train a lightweight linear projector to map the fixed vector into a smaller student's residual space. Student-side training uses only final-answer cross-entropy on a small subset of task training examples; it requires neither teacher outputs nor intermediate solution traces. We select the student injection layer and intervention scale on a labeled support set and report results on the disjoint remainder of each evaluation split. On GSM8K and MATH, the projected vector improves base students by 10.37-21.98 accuracy points across the evaluated teacher-student settings. On four code-generation benchmarks, the Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct student gains 3.23-4.67 pass@1 points, while the base Qwen2.5-7B student gains up to 9.65 points. These results show that a teacher-side reasoning vector can be reused across smaller students with different residual dimensions through projector-only adaptation.
